characterization_methods.key_findings: Very coarse equiaxed polygonal grains with a few straight parallel annealing twin bands and scattered dark pores; annealed microstructure with coarse grain size.

characterization_methods.purpose: determine alloy chemical composition including H, O, N

characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS 472 ± 5.4 MPa, YS 428 ± 6.5 MPa, total elongation 8 ± 1.4% (average of three tests).

comparative_performance.benchmark_process_id: AIMFC (air induction melting with flux cover) and VIM

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 80-mm-diameter Fe-7Al AIM ingot; the Fe-7Al AIM ingot was sound, free from hydrogen gas porosity and free from microcracks.
80-mm-diameter ingot preheated in a hearth furnace at 1373 K for 1 h, then hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature.

24-mm-thick forged billets preheated at 1373 K for 1 h and hot rolled by 50% with 1-mm reduction in thickness per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes under similar conditions as preheating; final hot-rolled plate thickness 12 mm.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Hot-rolled plate with final thickness 12 mm; each hardness data point is the average of five measurements; each tensile data point is the average of three tests.

defects.porosity: scattered dark pores observed in the optical micrograph

structures.overall_structure: Annealed microstructure with coarse grain size: very coarse equiaxed polygonal grains with a few straight parallel annealing twin bands and scattered dark pores (residual porosity/second-phase particles).

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the Fe-7Al AIM ingot (Table I): Al 7.22, Si 0.20, Mn 0.056, S 0.0075, C 0.021, O 0.0200, H 0.0052, N 0.02 wt.%.
The Fe-7Al alloy ingots produced by AIM were sound and free from hydrogen gas porosity and microcracks, unlike Fe-9Al AIM ingots which exhibited extensive gas porosity.
Hardness data indicate that the melting process (AIM, AIMFC, VIM) has no influence on the hardness of both Fe-7 wt.% and 9 wt.% Al alloys.
Aluminum recovery was excellent (95-98%) during AIMFC and VIM compared with plain AIM (the AIM recovery value itself is not reported).
